newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha rises, inter-month spreads narrower.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha rises, inter-month spreads narrower.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha firmed in afternoon trade on Thursday, lifted by overnight crudes, which surged on news that Russian President Boris Yeltsin must remain in hospital for the week recovering from pneumonia, traders said.

Offers for second-half March open-specification naphtha were heard at $243.00 per tonne, while bids were notionally quoted at around $241.50. It was assessed at $240.00/241.00 in late afternoon trade on Tuesday. The Tokyo oil products market was closed on Wednesday for a national holiday.
Open-spec naphtha for first-half April was indicated at about $239.50/241.00 in Thursday afternoon trade.
Inter-month naphtha spreads slightly narrowed, with second-half March/second-half April discussed at plus $4.00/5.00, against late Tuesday's levels of plus $4.50/5.50.

In low-sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) trading, most Indonesian cargoes allocated for January lifting had been sold, with about 1.8 million barrels destined for South Korea and some 1.4 million for Japan.
The remaining some 300,000 barrels of the total 3.5 million barrels initially allocated for January was believed to have been sold to India, fuel oil traders said.
